//imports: @wordroom/shared is consumed straight from source - no build step, no copy, no fork.
Its modules import each other with explicit .js specifiers (TypeScript's NodeNext
convention). Deno resolves those literally, so each one is remapped to its .ts twin
below. Relative import-map keys normalise against this file, and the specifiers inside
index.ts normalise against packages/shared/src, to the same URL - so they match.
This is exact and stable; the alternative (--sloppy-imports) is an unstable flag that
the deployed edge runtime is not guaranteed to honour.
//minimumDependencyAge: npm versions here are pinned to the ones already in pnpm-lock.yaml, so Deno's age gate would block a version the app is already using.

tasks.check: deno check _shared/*.ts _shared/guess-list/index.ts _tests/*.ts create-room/index.ts join-room/index.ts get-puzzle/index.ts submit-guess/index.ts reveal/index.ts leave-room/index.ts leave-room/leave.ts
